slo_title: Understand Doubly Linked Lists - Deletion at the Middle

mcq.q: What happens if you delete a node in the middle of a doubly linked list

options.A: The previous node’s next pointer is updated to point to the next node
options.B: The head pointer is always updated
options.C: The tail pointer is always updated
options.D: The next node’s previous pointer is set to NULL

mcq.answer_text: The previous node’s next pointer is updated to point to the next node

mcq.q: When deleting the last node in a doubly linked list, which pointers should be updated

options.A: Only the previous pointer of the last node
options.B: The previous pointer of the last node and the next pointer of the new last node

mcq.answer_text: The previous pointer of the last node and the next pointer of the new last node

mcq.q: Which case does NOT require special handling when deleting a node in a doubly linked list

options.C: Deleting a node in the middle
options.D: Deleting when the list is empty

mcq.answer_text: Deleting a node in the middle

mcq.q: What is the time complexity of deleting the first or last node in a doubly linked list
What happens when deleting the first node in a doubly linked list with more than one node

options.A: The head pointer is updated to point to the next node
options.C: The previous pointer of the new head is not modified
options.D: The next pointer of the old head is not modified

mcq.answer_text: The head pointer is updated to point to the next node
